rounds.headline: Two blockers and a keyboard trap. The planning drawer was white on white with no seam, so it sliced the Waiting column mid-word and erased Done entirely. The card's state rules were declared after its interaction rules at equal specificity, so Done and Next cards had no focus ring at all. And the completion circle, the one thing the board exists to do, was a bare span with no keyboard path.

worst.problem: The completion circle is not a control. It is a span: not focusable, no role, no aria state, no keyboard path, no active state. Its only feedback fires on hover of the whole card, so the circle looks armed while the cursor is 300px away.
worst.done: It is now a button with checkbox semantics, named by the task, with a 32px hit area that does not grow the 18px circle, and its own hover, active and focus. The card hints; the control answers one step darker.

worst.problem: `.card[data-done]` and `.card[data-next]` redeclare box-shadow after `:hover` and `:focus-visible` at equal specificity, so later wins. On the resting board the five Done cards and the milestone card have no hover edge, and because `outline: none` survives, no visible focus ring either.
worst.done: Every ring on a card now runs through one `--card-ring` custom property. States set only the token; hover, focus, selection and drag are declared last.

worst.problem: The planning drawer is white, on the same inset, with the same radius, with no ring, no shadow and no scrim, sitting on a white sheet that does not move. Waiting is cut mid-word, Done and its five cards vanish with no cue they exist.
worst.done: The sheet moves over and the ink floor shows through an 18px gutter, which draws the seam with the product's own elevation rule. The board switches to a scrolling track so no column is sliced, and the dock re-centres on the board it serves.

worst.problem: The dense header reads '5 of 32 done' while the Done tray immediately below it is labelled 9 and renders nine ticked cards. The board contradicts itself by four tasks in the one state that exists to prove it survives peak season.
worst.done: Every header fact is derived from the rendered task set. The total, the done count, the overdue count and the unscheduled count now all come from one accessor, and the empty state falls out of the same expression.

worst.problem: `.cardDots` sits at `opacity: 0` with pointer events live. On desktop a keyboard user tabs into a card and the focus ring paints on an invisible button. On touch, where hover never fires, the coarse rule inflates that invisible button to a 44x44 target.
worst.done: A control at zero opacity is now inert. The menu reveals on hover, focus-within and its own focus, and on a coarse pointer it is simply present and quieter.

worst.problem: One board scan carried four grammars for one fact: an elapsed duration, a deictic, a weekday and a date. The same state had two names in one frame: the header said '1 overdue', the card said '2 days late'.
worst.done: One grammar. Every chip states the day the work is due, formatted from real dates in the fixture against the pinned review clock. Lateness is carried entirely by the fill, which is what the direction claimed all along.

rounds.headline: Five of the seven seats independently found the same defect: the card's actions button was an opaque white square painting over content. On touch it severed every title mid-word; on hover it whited out most of the date chip, including the filled overdue chip the whole palette argument rests on.

worst.problem: On coarse pointers the menu is a permanently visible 44x44 button with a white fill, over a title row that reserves no space for it. In the 390px frame all three visible titles are severed mid-word with no ellipsis.
worst.done: Reserving a gutter fixed it and cost the title a whole line, so the answer is structural instead. The top-right of a card belongs to the time fact; the menu moved to the end of the foot row where the card's other quiet facts already live. Nothing moves when it appears, and it can never paint on content.

worst.problem: Drag is the board's defining gesture and it exists only for a pointer. There is no keyboard route for moving a task between columns, and at rest no card says it is draggable at all.
worst.done: Cards gained a grab cursor, and the keyboard move is specified, drawn and announced: space picks a card up into a lift without the tilt, the arrows walk it between columns. It has its own specimen on the card sheet.

worst.problem: Opening Planning silently deletes a status column. Five trays at 238px need 1190px inside the 884px the drawer leaves, so Waiting is sliced mid-word and Done is gone entirely with no cue it exists.
worst.done: Five trays now fit the narrowed board, and whatever still runs past the edge snaps and dissolves rather than being guillotined. The same edge treatment turns on wherever the board overflows, which is every width below 1200.

worst.problem: The board's grid row sizes to the tallest column, so every tray stretches to it and the tray's own overflow rule can never fire. Columns cannot scroll independently: reaching the foot of To do drags Done out of view.
worst.done: Each column is its own scroller now, and the dock's clearance sits at the foot of every one of them rather than once at the foot of the tallest.

worst.problem: Every spine item and every view tab is an anchor with no href. An anchor without href carries no role, so the product's entire navigation was a row of focusable generics inside a nav containing no links, and no element carried aria-current.
worst.done: They are buttons with accessible names and aria-current, with a reset so the change costs no pixels. The phone rule also stopped hiding tiles by matching their tooltip text.

worst.problem: Three of five columns state the same fact twice, three lines apart. Done reads 'Finished work stays visible.' then 'Finished work stays here, so you can see it.'
worst.done: One source per column. The tray note says what the column is for; the empty line says only that there is nothing in it, and only To do leads with an instruction, so an empty board has exactly one first move.

rounds.headline: UX rose to 8.0 and the minimum rose again, but UI composition dropped, because a new dominant defect surfaced that four of seven seats found independently: the dock and its scrim were erasing each column's Add task row. A panel that only ever goes up is not looking hard enough.

worst.problem: The dock is the largest floating object in the composition and it was placed with no regard for what sits beneath it. It erased the Add task row in two to four of five columns in every desktop frame, and half-dissolved a live card at peak density. The scrim existed only to blur the damage.
worst.done: The dock's band is reserved in real layout and the scrim is deleted. Nothing can sit under the dock any more, so every column gets its foot back, its rule runs to the sheet's edge, and the columns gain height rather than lose it.

worst.problem: A browser line clamp cuts at the character, so cards read 'dinner 5.30p...' and 'before we hold th...'. It is the one defect visible in every populated frame and it is exactly what separates typeset copy from text poured into a container.
worst.done: The renderer trims to the last whole word by binary search, keeps the full string on the element for the tooltip and for assistive technology, and the title lost the percentage floor that was pushing date chips off the card's edge.

worst.problem: Nothing anywhere on the board stated today's date, so every time chip floated without an anchor. The loudest object in the product, the filled ink overdue chip, said only '14 Jul': an operator could not tell two days late from two months.
worst.done: The header states today, first, and the season counter names the season it counts through rather than floating as an unexplained ordinal.

worst.problem: The direction's central claim is that status is carried by ink density and fill. That channel is entirely presentational: the chip's accessible name was a bare date, so overdue, due today and milestone were indistinguishable to anyone not looking at the screen.
worst.done: A visually hidden prefix now carries the same fact in words, and the trays became named regions with real headings instead of nameless sections that contributed nothing to the accessibility tree.

worst.problem: Every card was a tab stop with two more focusable children, so crossing the dense board was roughly ninety-six tab presses.
worst.done: One roving tab stop per column. Tab crosses the whole board in five presses and the arrows walk the column.

worst.problem: The account chip read DO, the initials of the words 'Demo operator', which belong to nobody on the board. Both cards in the Waiting column opened with the word Waiting, under a tray already headed WAITING and described as held by a reply.
worst.done: The operator is Orla, so the chip reads OR. The Waiting titles say what is being waited on rather than restating their own container.
